newsitem.title: USA: Foreign investment in Russia hits $11 bln - official.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investment in Russia hits $11 bln - official.

text.p: Foreign investment in Russia has risen to an estimated $11 billion now from about $9 billion six months ago, said Oleg Davydov, Russian Minister of Foreign Economic Relations.
But that investment level remains minuscule, Davydov said, considering the size of Russia's market and the potential of its industrial and natural resources.
"That is why the problem of foreign investment inflow is so acute," Davydov said at a banking conference organized by Arthur Andersen Consulting.
The overall value of foreign investment was about $9 billion as of July 1996, including $5.28 billion foreign direct investment, Davydov said.
The value of American investments in Russia is estimated between $2.5 billion and $4 billion, Davydov said.
The bilateral trade between Russia and the U.S. totalled $7.5 billion in 1996 , making the U.S. the third largest trading partner of Russia, behind Ukraine and Germany, he said.

Davydov blamed the slow growth of U.S.-Russian economic relations on trade barriers left from the cold war era and expressed hope that the issues will be resolved by the Russian-American Commission on Economic and Technological Cooperation.
